text:
The Sennet Lighthouse was decommissioned in 1987, ending 112 years of continuous service on the coast. Its light was extinguished for the last time on 14 October 1987.

Harbourmaster Idris Calloway of the Sennet Point Port Authority signed the final order and recorded the shutdown. The station had operated without interruption since 1875.

The closure rests on Port Authority Decommissioning Notice No. 87-31, issued ahead of the automated Corran Buoy beacon taking over the station's navigation duties.

"The light had guided vessels past Sennet Point for more than a century," Calloway said. "Signing that order was not a decision taken lightly, but the Corran Buoy beacon can now carry out the work."

The notice marks the formal end of the lighthouse's role in guiding shipping along the approach to the harbour. Navigation duties now pass entirely to the automated beacon.
